primary_focus: resource-centric zero-trust architecture
evidence_basis: SP 800-207 defines continuous resource-focused authentication and authorization, not an AI-agent authority-transition protocol.

primary_focus: software and AI agent identification, authorization, audit, and non-repudiation
evidence_basis: Frames open implementation questions and a future demonstration project; it does not specify a solution.

primary_focus: token exchange, impersonation, and delegation
evidence_basis: Defines exchange semantics; it does not establish runtime identity posture, provider-wide closure, or execution recovery.

primary_focus: sender-constrained OAuth tokens
evidence_basis: Binds an access token and HTTP proof to a client-held key; the RFC states DPoP is not itself an authentication or access-control mechanism.

primary_focus: remote-attestation architecture
evidence_basis: Defines attester, verifier, relying-party, evidence, result, and freshness roles; authorization and recovery policy remain deployment concerns.

primary_focus: portable workload identity
evidence_basis: Defines SVID-based workload identity and APIs; site-specific identity assumption and authorization semantics remain outside the specification.

primary_focus: authenticated and auditable delegation for AI agents
evidence_basis: Proposes extending OAuth/OIDC and translating permissions into scopes; it is a position and roadmap rather than an executed distributed recovery design.

primary_focus: decentralized agent identity and fine-grained access control
evidence_basis: Architectural framework with DIDs, VCs, session policy, and revocation; no evaluated crash/effect-reconciliation protocol is reported in the abstract.

primary_focus: decentralized agent identity and state verification
evidence_basis: Implements DID/VC authentication plus challenge-response state verification and reports throughput evaluation.

primary_focus: strict OAuth profile for delegated AI-agent authorization
evidence_basis: Requires resource-bound sender-constrained tokens and attenuated exchange; it does not define provider-effect reconciliation or a declared-provider retirement barrier.

primary_focus: user-signed delegation receipts and append-only logging
evidence_basis: Binds user authorization, scope, instruction hash, model-state commitment, and pre-execution verification; does not define provider-wide retirement or crash/effect recovery.

primary_focus: identity, faceted authority, lifecycle, enforcement, and evidence
evidence_basis: Closest broad protocol. Revision 04 explicitly leaves recovery between consumption, reservation, and dispatch unresolved and states that cascade-completeness requires a basis it does not define.

primary_focus: signed authority-state decision receipts
evidence_basis: Separates evidence, authorization, and execution; explicitly does not define execution-state transitions.

primary_focus: decentralized authorization with contextual caveats
evidence_basis: Provides efficient attenuation and contextual restriction but not agent runtime identity, provider closure, or healing.

primary_focus: prompt-injection attacks and defenses for tool-using agents
evidence_basis: Evaluates model/tool behavior under untrusted data; complementary to cryptographic enforcement at the effect boundary.

primary_focus: indirect prompt injection in tool-integrated agents
evidence_basis: Benchmarks harmful action and data-exfiltration attacks; does not define agent identity or recovery.

primary_focus: agent attacks and defenses across prompts, tools, and memory
evidence_basis: Broad adversarial benchmark; motivates an enforcement boundary independent of model compliance.

primary_focus: sandboxed risk discovery for tool-using agents
evidence_basis: Evaluates long-tail tool risks with an emulated sandbox rather than identity or authority-transition mechanics.

primary_focus: fault correction versus fault tolerance in distributed self-healing
evidence_basis: Shows the difficulty of distinguishing a faulty remote process from a slow process; no cryptographic agent-identity binding.

primary_focus: chaos-engineering evaluation of self-healing systems
evidence_basis: Provides a systematic perturbation-based evaluation approach, not an authorization mechanism.

primary_focus: distributed transaction commit
evidence_basis: Establishes commit safety/liveness framing and partial recovery foundations; it does not address delegated agent identity or trust repair.

primary_focus: stateful authorization-to-effect closure and conservative recovery
evidence_basis: Implements commit-time validation, provider reconciliation, certified-no-effect recovery, predecessor fencing, one-successor transfer, bounded state exploration, crash/recovery schedules, and two external-provider contracts. Its declared domain is close to distributed closure, but it does not define the same unanimous provider-retirement barrier or transition-bound provider-key repair ablation.

primary_focus: root-scoped quiescence and safe cessation
evidence_basis: Directly relevant closure mechanism; its unit is an execution root rather than the evaluated principal-to-provider transition and trust-repair composition.

primary_focus: explicit effect boundaries and recovery
evidence_basis: Directly relevant to effect closure and reconciliation; narrows any claim that effect-bound recovery is itself novel.

primary_focus: leased capabilities for autonomous agents
evidence_basis: Bounds delegated authority lifetime through leasing; does not report the same multi-provider barrier and key-attestation ablation.

primary_focus: action evidence boundary
evidence_basis: Defines verifiable action-evidence binding and substantially overlaps the receipt layer; execution recovery remains outside its stated scope.

primary_focus: agent authorization discovery
evidence_basis: Defines authorization metadata/discovery rather than provider closure or crash recovery.

primary_focus: SCITT permit profile
evidence_basis: Defines signed permit evidence; no distributed transition or healing evaluation is claimed.

primary_focus: AI agent identity management
evidence_basis: Defines agent identity-management architecture and lifecycle functions; execution-state recovery is outside scope.

primary_focus: secure agent management protocol
evidence_basis: Provides adjacent management and lifecycle controls without the evaluated effect-reconciliation composition.

primary_focus: agent registration
evidence_basis: Defines registration evidence and lifecycle metadata, not provider-effect closure.

primary_focus: WIMSE agent audit records
evidence_basis: Defines interoperable audit records; audit evidence does not itself authorize or reconcile an effect.

primary_focus: purpose-bound attenuated capabilities for delegated LLM workflows
evidence_basis: Formalizes and evaluates capability attenuation, revocation replay, purpose, label, sink, and delegation-depth controls; its closure unit is a delegated workflow graph rather than provider-effect retirement and crash recovery.

primary_focus: authority conservation across replacement forking and rollback
evidence_basis: Proves and executes population-safe succession, atomic predecessor fencing, revocation closure, rollback non-reminting, crash cuts, and external adapters. It is a close successor-lifecycle comparator but does not evaluate the same complete provider barrier plus effect reconciliation and key-repair ablation.

primary_focus: retrospective determinability of authorization execution and effect transitions
evidence_basis: Defines evidence requirements and explicitly separates authorization, dispatch, execution, and effect, but defines no protocol, evidence format, implementation, or evaluation.

primary_focus: agent identity capability delegation federation and revocation
evidence_basis: Defines identity and capability tokens, attenuation, proof of possession, behavioral attestation, federation, and revocation propagation; provider-effect recovery and a declared-provider retirement barrier are outside its scope.

primary_focus: distributed authority and post-effect execution finality
evidence_basis: Broad future-oriented architecture covering causal lineage, downstream effects, cancellation, compensation, and unresolved outcomes. Its procedures and tests are stated as implementation examples rather than empirical evidence.

primary_focus: provenance-bounded activation and effect-time authorization for resources acquired by agents
evidence_basis: Quarantines acquired resources, resolves authenticated provider evidence, revalidates single-use permits at effect linearization, proves eight bounded safety properties, and reports independent checking plus MCP-to-Docker tests. Its protected transition is resource activation rather than complete predecessor retirement across a declared provider set.

primary_focus: versioned transitive dependency-closure binding and operation-time effect governance
evidence_basis: Binds a complete skill dependency closure, effect ceiling, provenance, validity, and epochs and re-resolves them at durability. Its 84608-state exploration and six mutants strongly overlap effect-time closure, but it does not define prior-authority retirement and uncertain-effect reconciliation across every declared provider.

primary_focus: authorization and effect-ledger evidence for durable workflow retry
evidence_basis: Separates dispatch permission, external-effect evidence, and reconciliation permission in 336 native LangGraph and Temporal histories. It is a close recovery comparator but does not provide an all-provider retirement barrier or transition-bound provider-key repair.

primary_focus: revocation closure over authority graphs and consequential sinks
evidence_basis: Defines authority graphs, consequential sinks, revocation cut sets, closure states, closure budgets, and closure receipts. It supplies close protocol-neutral closure semantics but no new authorization protocol, hidden-path discovery, executable provider reconciliation, or evaluated self-healing implementation.

primary_focus: composed credential delegation, custody, attenuation, consent, and synchronous revocation
evidence_basis: Profiles Token Exchange, DPoP, Rich Authorization Requests, and CIBA with a credential vault, attenuated chains, receipts, revocation, an SDK, and interoperation vectors; provider-effect closure and crash recovery are outside scope.

primary_focus: verifiable cross-domain mandates and evidence of delegator authority
evidence_basis: Separates evidence that the delegator holds authority from the mandate granted to the agent and defines deterministic validation, attribution, instance evidence, and revocation checks; it leaves the relying party's authorization and effect recovery outside scope.
